title: Morphological and Molecular Characterization of Two Stylonychid Ciliates Isolated in Austria
content: Integrative taxonomy is important for accurate identification of ciliate species and understanding of their evolutionary relationships. This study investigated two freshwater hypotrich ciliates isolated in Austria using morphology, cyst structure and two molecular markers (rDNA and COI gene). Stylonychia ammermanni is characterized as follows: body size 164 × 70 µm in vivo, 15–21 left and 24–35 right marginal cirri, 30–50 adoral membranelles, and no ring-shaped structures on cysts. Stylonychia vorax resembles Tetmemena pustulata in morphology, rDNA and COI and we therefore synonymize it. Phylogenetic analyses of the SSU rDNA and ITS2 secondary structure nest T. pustulata within the Tetmemena and S. ammermanni in a Stylonychia complex, respectively. We also show that although Tetmemena species can be delimited by morphology, the ITS and COI genes are more variable than the SSU rRNA gene and allow for species discrimination. However, this study showed cyst morphological differences and genetic divergence between S. ammermanni populations of Italy and Austria. This recommends reexamination of cyst structure and molecular data of S. ammermanni, particularly for the type material.
